correctness.rationale: For every k>=2 and m>=1, the exact root-anchored distance-power Gram matrix decomposes into k(m-1) positive leaf-difference eigenvalues, k-1 copies of a two-dimensional antisymmetric block, and one two-dimensional symmetric block. The cross-branch kernel is negative semidefinite for 1<=p<=2 by the convergent Laplace-Gamma representation, strictly negative on the two distinct root-depth features when 1<p<2. Thus the symmetric 2x2 principal-minor and determinant test is necessary and sufficient. At p=1 the determinant is 1; for k>=3 the determinant is negative at h_k<2; for k=2,m>1 it is negative just below 2. Strictness below any later admissible exponent rules out two interior roots and proves the sharp phase. The endpoint kernel is one-dimensional because the other blocks are positive definite; Schoenberg supplies exact affine embedding rank. The sole exception (k,m)=(2,1) is the Euclidean five-vertex path. Direct differentiation and an implicit-function argument give the fixed-k large-m coefficient c_k=k log(32/27)+log(27/16)>0. An independent BFS distance-and-spectrum checker passed 448 eigenvalue comparisons, 64 endpoint multiplicity checks, 448 phase checks and 21 large-m checks. Finite checks alone do not establish the all-parameter conclusion.

value.rationale: The object is the natural two-generation spherically symmetric tree with prescribed two levels of branching. Its supremal p-negative type is an intrinsic invariant controlling isometric Hilbert embeddings of metric snowflakes, and its endpoint equality-support dimension is a structural geometry quantity. In the prior literature, even the binary depth-two case was calculated numerically, while generic finite-metric formulae require large nonlinear determinants. A two-by-two sharp formula for every k and m, an exact one-dimensional critical equality ray (except the precisely identified path), and a sharp 1/m approach to the tree lower limit give a complete motivated family result and a useful branch-kernel structural lemma. This is substantially more than a small-case recomputation or mere software validation.
